title: Machine-readable result transport still requires host JSON
observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, and subprocess-fallback execution adjudication are MNCS-owned. The Rust bootstrap CLI still serializes the external action-facing TestResult/CheckResult JSON and artifact paths; Python preserves process supervision, typed projection, raw diagnostics, and compatibility transport.
why_insufficient: The Test process and execution decision slice now runs in one native application call, but the complete cross-repository evidence protocol, including bounded strings/bytes and canonical JSON encoding, is not yet an application-level MNCS library surface.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py emits mncs.test-result/1 and mncs.check-result/1 after receiving the typed record from mncs-embed batch execution.
desired_direction: A versioned native serialization/protocol library for bounded structured results, with explicit text/bytes policy and lossless adapter projections.
workaround: The Rust toolchain performs the external structured JSON projection. Python remains responsible for process supervision, typed-value projection, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport; it no longer classifies subprocess transport or decoded execution outcomes.
